Recipes.Diagnosis: The bench legs have split. The keeper cannot tension a clean wrap on the loose frame. Brace it with two sound timber lengths.
Recipes.RepairedText: New timber braces hold the dressing bench firm. The keeper can prepare field dressings.

Recipes.Diagnosis: A split in the fired lining lets the drawn water drain through the rim. Pack the gap with fire clay.
Recipes.RepairedText: The lining is repaired. A fresh clay seam holds the drawn water.

Recipes.Diagnosis: The wooden frame has sagged. The gate hangs open and cannot swing on its broken braces.
Recipes.RepairedText: The frame is repaired. New timber braces let the gate swing and latch.

Recipes.Diagnosis: A frayed end hangs from the spindle. The bucket cannot be lowered or retrieved until its line is replaced.
Recipes.RepairedText: The well line is repaired. New knotflax cord carries the bucket.

Recipes.Diagnosis: A split crosses the fired pan. Pulp leaks onto the coals before the grain can be wrapped. Pack the split with two fire clay.
Recipes.RepairedText: Fresh clay closes the split. The batch pan can hold a paid expedition meal.

Recipes.Diagnosis: The lower rail has buckled against its post. Two sound lengths will brace the hinges and let the closed wicket swing.
Recipes.RepairedText: New timber braces hold the hinges true. The wicket can be opened and closed.

Recipes.Diagnosis: The working metal is damaged. A steel blade can replace or brace the failing edge.
Recipes.RepairedText: The equipment is repaired and its combat penalty is removed.

Recipes.Diagnosis: The wooden striking end is split. A sound timber length can brace it.
Recipes.RepairedText: The equipment is repaired and its combat penalty is removed.

Recipes.Diagnosis: The protective leather is torn. Fresh binding can close the failed seam.
Recipes.RepairedText: The equipment is repaired and its combat penalty is removed.
